title: Native Ad Creative Best Practices
content: Native advertising performs best when creative elements blend seamlessly with surrounding content. Key guidelines: 1) Use editorial-style headlines that inform rather than sell. 2) Match image style to publisher content. 3) Include clear brand attribution. 4) Test multiple headline variations — we see 30-40% CTR improvement from headline optimization alone. 5) For StackAdapt campaigns, leverage dynamic creative optimization (DCO) to automatically test combinations. Recommended aspect ratios: 1200x627 for feed placements, 600x600 for social-style units.

title: CTV Campaign Setup & Optimization Guide
content: Connected TV campaigns require different optimization approaches than display. Setup: 1) Target minimum 15-second non-skippable spots for brand campaigns. 2) Use frequency capping at 3-5 exposures per household per week. 3) Layer contextual targeting with genre-level content alignment. Optimization: Monitor completion rates (target >90%), adjust dayparting based on viewing patterns (primetime 7-11pm typically 2x reach), and use cross-device attribution to track downstream conversions. Budget allocation: Start with 60% reach-optimized, 40% completion-optimized.

title: Retargeting Window Optimization
content: Retargeting effectiveness decays exponentially with time since last engagement. Recommended windows by funnel stage: Site visitors (general) — 7-14 days for best ROAS; Product viewers — 3-7 days, these show strongest purchase intent; Cart abandoners — 1-3 days, use aggressive frequency (5-7/day) with discount messaging; Past purchasers — 30-60 days for cross-sell, 60-90 days for replenishment. Always exclude recent converters (7-day suppression minimum). For StackAdapt campaigns, use the recency decay bidding modifier to automatically decrease bids as the retargeting window ages.

title: Viewability Rate Improvement Playbook
content: Viewability directly impacts campaign effectiveness and client satisfaction. Current platform average: 68%. Target: >75%. Actions to improve: 1) Avoid below-the-fold inventory — use Above The Fold (ATF) targeting where available. 2) Prefer larger ad units (300x250 outperforms 728x90 by 15pts). 3) Implement pre-bid viewability filters at 60% threshold minimum. 4) Exclude low-viewability domains from your blocklist (review quarterly). 5) Use StackAdapt's predictive viewability scoring to bid higher on likely-viewable impressions. Impact: Every 10pt viewability increase correlates with 8-12% CTR improvement.

title: Audience Segment Layering Strategy
content: Layering audience segments creates precision targeting but reduces scale. Best practices: Start broad (contextual + demographic), then narrow based on performance. Layer order: 1) Behavioral intent signals (highest value), 2) Demographic qualifiers, 3) Contextual alignment. Never layer more than 3 segments simultaneously — beyond this, reach drops below actionable levels. For lookalike audiences, use 1% seed for precision, 3-5% for scale. Combine first-party data with third-party behavioral signals for strongest performance. Monitor overlap rates between segments — >30% overlap means consolidation opportunity.

title: Budget Pacing & Delivery Optimization
content: Proper budget pacing prevents overspend early in campaigns and underspend at end. Rules: 1) Use accelerated delivery only for time-sensitive campaigns (flash sales, events). 2) Standard pacing (even distribution) is default for all performance campaigns. 3) If a campaign is >15% behind pace by mid-flight, increase bids by 10-20% rather than switching to accelerated. 4) Set daily caps at 120% of ideal daily spend to allow for high-opportunity days while maintaining weekly budget. 5) For monthly budgets, allocate 40% to first half, 60% to second half (learning period optimization). Monitor hourly delivery curves for anomalies.

title: Cross-Device Attribution Setup
content: Cross-device attribution captures the full customer journey across smartphones, tablets, desktop, and CTV. Setup requirements: 1) Implement StackAdapt universal pixel on all advertiser pages. 2) Enable deterministic matching via hashed email where available. 3) Configure attribution windows: 24hr view-through, 7-day click-through for display; 14-day for CTV. 4) Use data-driven attribution (DDA) model for multi-touch campaigns rather than last-click. 5) Report on both assisted and last-touch conversions. Expected impact: Cross-device typically reveals 20-35% more conversions than single-device tracking.

title: Programmatic Video Completion Rate Guide
content: Video completion rate (VCR) is the primary success metric for video campaigns. Benchmarks: 15s pre-roll >85%, 30s mid-roll >70%, 6s bumper >95%. Optimization tactics: 1) Front-load the brand message in first 5 seconds. 2) Use captions — 85% of mobile video is watched with sound off. 3) For longer formats (>15s), use storytelling arc: hook (0-3s), problem (3-8s), solution (8-12s), CTA (12-15s). 4) Implement VPAID vs VAST carefully — VPAID enables interactivity but reduces fill rate by 15-20%. 5) A/B test thumbnail frames — first frame is critical for autoplay environments.

title: Client Retention: Early Warning Signals
content: Client churn indicators appear 60-90 days before actual cancellation. Key signals to monitor: 1) Spend decline >20% month-over-month without seasonal explanation. 2) Campaign pause rate increasing — more than 3 campaigns paused in 30 days. 3) Platform login frequency dropping below 2x per week. 4) Support ticket volume increasing (frustration signal). 5) Contract renewal discussions starting late (within 30 days of expiry). 6) Performance degradation without advertiser action to optimize. Action plan: Trigger QBR (Quarterly Business Review) when 2+ signals detected. Assign senior AM for proactive outreach. Present optimization roadmap with guaranteed performance improvements.

title: Revenue Expansion Playbook: Upsell Strategies
content: Top expansion opportunities by client tier: Gold tier — CTV channel expansion (avg 40% spend increase), programmatic guaranteed for premium inventory. Silver tier — add native channel (25-30% incremental), lookalike audience scaling. Bronze tier — upgrade to managed service (50-70% spend increase with AM support). Timing: Propose expansion after 2+ consecutive months of meeting/exceeding KPIs. Lead with data: show performance headroom, untapped audience segments, and competitor activity. Average expansion deal: $45K incremental annual spend. Close rate: 35% when data-led, 12% without performance proof.

title: Contextual Targeting Without Cookies
content: As third-party cookies deprecate, contextual targeting becomes critical. StackAdapt contextual capabilities: 1) Page-level classification across 300+ IAB content categories. 2) Sentiment analysis — target positive content environments. 3) Keyword inclusion/exclusion lists for granular control. 4) Custom context models trained on advertiser-specific content affinity. Performance comparison: Contextual targeting achieves 85-90% of cookie-based behavioral targeting performance while being fully privacy-compliant. Best for: brand safety-conscious advertisers, regulated industries (pharma, finance), European campaigns under GDPR strict enforcement.

title: Frequency Cap Optimization Framework
content: Over-frequency wastes budget and annoys users; under-frequency fails to create awareness. Recommended caps by objective: Awareness campaigns — 5-8 impressions per user per week. Consideration — 3-5 per week. Conversion/retargeting — 7-10 per day (high intent justifies higher frequency). Cross-channel considerations: Set HOLISTIC frequency caps across all campaigns for same advertiser to prevent bombardment. Monitor frequency distribution: if >30% of impressions serve to users at max cap, your reach is too narrow — expand targeting. Diminishing returns typically begin after the 6th exposure within a 7-day window.

title: DSP Algorithm Training: Bid Optimization
content: StackAdapt's ML bidding algorithms require proper training data. Guidelines: 1) Allow 7-day learning period before evaluating performance — algorithms need 50+ conversions to optimize effectively. 2) Don't change targeting or budgets >20% during learning. 3) Use CPA or ROAS goals rather than manual CPM bids for performance campaigns. 4) Provide accurate conversion values for value-based bidding. 5) Ensure pixel fires are clean (no duplicates, proper attribution windows). 6) For new campaigns with no history, start with awareness-optimized delivery for 3-5 days, then switch to conversion optimization once learning is complete.

title: Quarterly Business Review Template
content: QBR structure for client retention and expansion: Slide 1 — Executive summary (30 seconds): highlight top KPI achievement and key recommendation. Slides 2-4 — Performance review: Show QoQ trends for primary KPIs (ROAS, CPA, reach). Include competitive benchmarks (anonymized platform averages by vertical). Slides 5-6 — Insights: Audience discoveries, creative performance leaders, channel mix analysis. Slide 7 — Roadmap: Next quarter plan with 3 concrete optimization initiatives. Slide 8 — Growth opportunity: Present one data-backed expansion proposal (new channel, audience, or budget increase). Deliver QBR within 10 business days of quarter close.

title: Brand Safety & Suitability Standards
content: Brand safety is non-negotiable for all campaigns. Minimum standards: 1) Enable pre-bid brand safety filtering (IAS or DoubleVerify integration). 2) Maintain global exclusion list: hate speech, adult content, illegal activity, violence, misinformation. 3) Advertiser-specific blocklists: competitors, controversial topics per industry. 4) News category handling: Block hard news for sensitive brands, allow for finance/tech advertisers. 5) Made-for-advertising (MFA) site blocking: Use StackAdapt's MFA detection to exclude low-quality inventory. 6) Post-campaign reporting: Include brand safety score in all client reports. Target: <0.5% unsafe impression rate.

title: Campaign Launch Checklist
content: Pre-launch verification (all campaigns): 1) Tracking: Pixel installed, test conversion firing, attribution window configured. 2) Creative: All sizes approved, click URLs validated, landing pages load <3s. 3) Targeting: Audience segments attached, geo-fencing verified, frequency caps set. 4) Budget: Daily/lifetime budget confirmed, pacing strategy selected. 5) Brand safety: Blocklist applied, pre-bid filtering enabled. 6) Measurement: Viewability provider active, conversion events defined. 7) Timeline: Flight dates match media plan, dayparting configured if applicable. Post-launch (24hr check): Delivery started, no error flags, initial metrics within expected range.

title: Data-Driven Creative Optimization
content: Leverage performance data to continuously improve creative assets. Framework: 1) Launch with minimum 3 creative variations per ad size. 2) After 1000 impressions per variation, identify statistical leader (95% confidence). 3) Pause underperformers, introduce new challengers. 4) Test one variable at a time: headline vs. image vs. CTA vs. color. 5) Winning patterns by channel: Display — bold CTAs, high-contrast images; Native — editorial headlines, lifestyle imagery; Video — first-3-second hook, clear brand identity. 6) Refresh creative every 2-3 weeks to combat ad fatigue. Monitor CTR decay curve — >15% decline signals refresh needed.

title: Lookalike Audience Scaling Methodology
content: Lookalike audiences are the primary scale lever for performance campaigns. Seed requirements: Minimum 1000 users in seed audience for reliable modeling. Higher quality seeds (purchasers > add-to-carts > site visitors) produce better lookalikes. Scaling path: Start at 1% lookalike (highest precision), test performance for 7 days. If CPA is within 20% of seed audience performance, expand to 3%. At 3%, if still performant, test 5%. Beyond 5%, performance typically degrades to near-prospecting levels. Combine lookalikes with contextual or behavioral layers for precision-at-scale. Refresh seed audiences monthly as customer profiles evolve.

title: Multi-Touch Attribution Model Selection
content: Attribution model selection significantly impacts reported performance and budget allocation decisions. Model comparison: Last-click — simple but heavily biased toward lower-funnel touchpoints. Favors search/retargeting. First-click — biased toward awareness tactics. Rarely recommended. Linear — equal credit across all touchpoints. Fair but doesn't account for impact differences. Time-decay — more credit to recent touchpoints. Good default for consideration campaigns. Data-driven (DDA) — ML-based, accounts for actual contribution. Recommended when sufficient conversion volume (>300/month). Position-based — 40/20/40 split (first, middle, last). Good compromise for full-funnel campaigns. StackAdapt recommendation: Use DDA for high-volume accounts, time-decay for mid-volume, last-click only for direct response.

title: Platform Health Monitoring Dashboard Guide
content: RevOps team daily monitoring checklist: 1) Platform-wide delivery: Total spend vs. forecast (variance >10% requires investigation). 2) Error rates: Campaign serving errors <0.1%, pixel fire failures <2%. 3) Pacing alerts: Campaigns >20% ahead/behind pace flagged automatically. 4) Client health dashboard: Review any accounts dropping below 60 engagement score. 5) Revenue at risk: Flag any Gold/Silver tier showing month-over-month decline. 6) Pipeline: Check deals with close dates within 14 days. Weekly: Review aggregate take-rate trends, identify compression. Monthly: Full revenue forecast vs. actual analysis, client tier movement tracking.
